item.title: Shenendehowa girls' volleyball beats Corning to claim NYSPHSAA Class AAA championship
item.description: Shenendehowa celebrates beating Corning in the NYSPHSAA Class AAA girls' volleyball championship match at Harding Mazzotti Arena on Saturday in Glens Falls. (Stephen Weaver) GLENS FALLS - All throughout Saturday night's NYSPHSAA Class AAA girls' volleyball championship match, Shenendehowa sophomore outside hitter got the same piece of advice from her coaches. "We were telling Mel all game, ‘Come on, a little bit faster, a little bit faster,'" Shenendehowa coach Lori Kessler said. In the biggest moment of her volleyball career, Tubbs was more than up to speed. The left-handed sophomore delivered three crucial kills down the stretch of the fourth set against Section 4's Corning, including the most important one of all. With the Mustangs a point away from a state championship, Tubbs got a perfect set from junior star Hadley Ennist and delivered a forceful swing. Her spike smacked off the hands of diving Corning libero Bella Gonzalez and onto the floor of Harding Mazzotti Arena. From there, it was celebration time for Shen with a 25-14, 21-25, 25-14, 25-19 win. "Going up there, I definitely knew it's all or nothing," Tubbs said. "Like, this is that final moment, I have to give everything I've got. I was just like, this is what every single practice, every single game of this whole season, it all led up to this moment." The win returned Shenendehowa to the top of New York girls' volleyball for the second time. The program won its first state title in 2022, then returned to the championship match in 2024 and finished as runners-up to Section 5's Fairport. In 2025, Shen reached the state final four but was eliminated after round-robin pool play. "The past few years, we've fallen short, lost in the finals, not quite made it there," Tubbs said. "This year, with our seniors, it was our final shot. It really means so much to finally put all those pieces together and finally bring it home for each other and, of course, coach Kessler." As they have been all season, in the state final the Mustangs were led by Ennist, the team's do-it-all superstar. The junior, who has verbally committed to play Division I volleyball at Old Dominion University, put up a staggering stat line Saturday night with 15 kills, 23 assists, nine digs and four blocks. She didn't come off the court once during the match. "She's playing defense. She's running offense. She's finishing points. She's putting up a block," Kessler said of Ennist's performance. "She's challenged some of the best outside hitters in the state this season because her block is so demanding. She's really doing it all for us." Corning provided a unique challenge for Shenendehowa thanks to the presence of two powerhouse middle blockers - 6-foot-5 Charlise Starns and 6-foot-2 Losseki Molingou. But more than that, since October he has been the head coach of Delhi Capitals, which makes Chennai Super Kings a side he now has to plan against rather than admire. Asked about the retirement by News18 Bangla , he paid tribute and then took the benefit. "It will be difficult to replace Dhoni at CSK. item.title: Elias Lindholm’s 1st NHL 4-goal game and 1st trick with Boston carries Bruins to 7-5 win over Caps
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 21: Elias Lindholm #28 of the Boston Bruins celebrates a win against the Washington Capitals at TD Garden on November 21, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. The Bruins won 7-5. (Photo by Rich Gagnon/Getty Images) Rich Gagnon BOSTON (AP) — Elias Lindholm had the first four-goal game of his NHL career to carry the Boston Bruins past the Washington Capitals 7-5 on Saturday. It was his first hat trick with Boston and the third of his career. David Pastrnak, Tanner Jeannot and Fraser Minten also scored for Boston. Charlie McAvoy added three assists to reach 301 for his career. Minten’s goal was an empty-netter. Jeremy Swayman made 30 saves and had a secondary assist on Lindholm’s second score at 8:54 of the second period that gave Boston a 4-2 lead. Alex Tuch, Tom Wilson, Pierre-Luc Dubois, Dylan Strome and Jakob Chychrun scored goals for the Capitals, who have lost five straight. Lindholm’s third came on a tip of Connor Clifton’s shot that moved Boston ahead 5-4 late in the second. Because it was tipped, most of the fans didn’t realize he completed the hat trick and only one hat was thrown onto the ice until about a half dozen came at the end of the period after his goal was announced. His fourth goal was on the tip of Pastrnak’s shot that popped over goalie Charlie Lindgren 4:07 into the third, prompting a delayed celebration with many more hats sailing onto the ice as Frankie Valli’s “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” played over the PA. Lindgren had 16 saves. Back home after ending a three-game losing streak with a victory at Detroit on Wednesday , the Bruins scored three times in the opening nine minutes of the second. Pastrnak circled with the puck in the Capitals’ zone before his wrister tied it at 2 just over two minutes into period. Jeannot’s tip-in made it 3-2 at 6:23. Lindholm split a pair of defensemen before flipping the puck into the net 2:31 later for his second. Lindholm’s first goal was a power-play score on a tip of Pastrnak’s shot. item.description: WASHINGTON — The Kansas City Current won their first NWSL Championship on Saturday with a defensive masterclass and a soccer rarity: an Olimpico. In the 54th minute of a feisty final against the Washington Spirit, Current midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo curled a corner kick directly into the net, silenced 19,365 rowdy Spirit fans and sparked wild celebrations in Kansas City. The so-called Olimpico, the colloquial term for a goal directly from a corner, was the decisive goal of a tight, tense, physical match. It descended into chaos in second-half stoppage time. Debinha added a second for Kansas City, which seemed to seal the match. A couple minutes later, the Spirit pulled a goal back, and then pushed maniacally for an equalizer. But, after multiple goal-mouth scrambles, they couldn’t find one. And at the final whistle, Current players and executives spilled onto the field to celebrate a dramatic 2-1 win. Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains, along with turf toe, during the Rams’ Week 9 game against Washington. Head coach Sean McVay had already suggested supporters should prepare for an extended absence. item.title: Kansas City crowned NWSL champions as Washington jinx strikes again
item.description: Kansas City Current players celebrate after Debinha scores to seal victory in the NWSL championship game against the Washington Spirit (Scott Taetsch) Kansas City Current defeated Washington Spirit 2-1 to be crowned NWSL champions for the first time on Saturday as Trinity Rodman's bid to avoid a third consecutive final defeat ended in bitter disappointment. Vanessa DiBernardo curled in a goal direct from a corner and Brazilian international Debinha added a second in stoppage time to set up Kansas City's victory. Rodman headed in a 98th-minute goal to pull one back for Spirit, but Kansas City held on for victory. It was another crushing loss for United States star Rodman and her Spirit team-mates, who were also beaten in the final in 2025 and 2024. Rodman, who was in tears at the final whistle, was knocked out of her stride early on at Washington's Audi Field. The 24-year-old was on the receiving end of a rugged aerial challenge from Kansas City's Laney Rouse after just five minutes and needed treatment on the sidelines. Rodman returned to the game grimacing in pain and clutching her shoulder after the incident but completed the game. The opening goal came early in the second half, with DiBernardo's in-swinging corner looping into the net after Kansas City's Kayla Sharples cleverly blocked Washington goalkeeper Sandy MacIver. Deep in stoppage time, Debinha added Current's second after a sweeping counter-attack, before Rodman's header was too little too late. The victory was Kansas City's first NWSL title after losing in the championship game to the Portland Thorns in 2022. rcw/js

item.title: WPIAL champions for 2026 season decided in Class 4A, 6A
item.description: The first two WPIAL football championships of the 2026 season were decided Saturday at Pine-Richland High School, where Central Catholic captured the Class 6A crown, and Montour secured the Class 4A title. The first two WPIAL football championships of the 2026 season were decided Saturday at Pine-Richland High School, where Central Catholic captured the Class 6A crown, and Montour secured the Class 4A title. Central Catholic defeated Canon-McMillan 57-7, while Montour defeated New Castle 31-27. With the victory, Central Catholic became the first program to three-peat in WPIAL Class 6A history. In the Class 4A contest, Montour overcame a fourth-quarter deficit against New Castle, leaning on its ground attack to secure the trophy in the final minute. In the Class 6A game, Central Catholic built an early 15-0 lead behind standout Chrys Black, who put the Vikings on the board first. Canon-McMillan vs. Central Catholic Canon-McMillan cut into the margin when quarterback Ty Jansma connected with Bryan Schmeltz on a 17-yard touchdown pass to make it 15-7. Central Catholic responded immediately. Roman Thompson broke outside and was pushed out at the Canon-McMillan 8-yard line, setting up an Owen Herrick touchdown pass to Connor Melnick to give the Vikings a 22-7 lead. The Vikings expanded their lead in the third quarter after attempting a fourth-and-3 conversion. Black broke a tackle and ran for a touchdown. Black finished with three touchdowns on the day, adding a 22-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to cap the 50-point victory. Central Catholic head coach Ryan Lehmeier praised the leadership of his senior players following the milestone win. “It just talks a lot about their character and their commitment to the program, and them holding the standard that we set high every single day,” Lehmeier said. “And I think they’ve been the ones that held the rest of the group accountable, and you’re able to accomplish things like this through having groups like them.” Montour vs. New Castle In the Class 4A championship, Montour opened the scoring when Archie Collins took a handoff for a 40-yard touchdown run. The Spartans then went to the air, extending their lead to 14-0 on a 17-yard pass from Brandon Bennett to Zander Stern. New Castle narrowed the margin on a 57-yard fumble recovery, but Bennett answered with a touchdown run to put Montour ahead 21-6. New Castle then launched a 21-3 scoring run, beginning with a touchdown run by Jermaine Walker to make it 21-14 at halftime. Montour extended its lead to 10 points with a field goal, but New Castle’s Marino Graham scored a touchdown to pull within three. Walker then scored his second touchdown with over seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, giving New Castle a 27-24 lead. Montour answered with a six-minute, 25-second drive that drained the clock. Bennett finished the drive with a 10-yard touchdown run with 42 seconds remaining, sealing the 31-27 championship win. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
